author: Max Blumenthal
description: Nintendo gave us a decent slice of gameplay during the 40th anniversary Zelda direct. But they did not show everything, on their website lies tons of additional footage that was not shown during the stream. We showcase all of it in one cohesive montage.
title: 6 Minutes Of Extra Ocarina Of Time Remake Gameplay

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Xbox Game Pass grows today with the addition of a popular Call of Duty game. New to the service from today, September 8, is 2020's Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. It's available on Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, and PC Game Pass, and the game supports cloud streaming as well.

Developed by Treyarch and Raven, Black Ops Cold War is set in Cold War-era 1981, with its campaign following Russell Adler as he and his team seek out a spy named Perseus. The game also has multiplayer, of course, along with Zombies.

Black Ops Cold War was a bit hit, becoming
title: Xbox Game Pass Adds A Great Call Of Duty Game Today

author: Jade King
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was always going to prove divisive. Whether it strove to be a faithful retelling or a bold reimagining like Final Fantasy 7 Remake, Zelda’s 3D debut is so beloved, so seminal, and so ingrained in our collective nostalgia that aiming to please everyone was always going to be impossible. Personally? I think it looks just fine. 

I was slightly underwhelmed by the fact that, aside from quality-of-life improvements and an essential modernization of certain gameplay mechanics, Nintendo is pretty much poised to deliver a 1:1 remake. The scale of characters, depth of locations, and overall scope of Link’s world is
title: Why Is Link The Worst-Looking Character In The Ocarina Of Time Remake?

author: Blair Marnell
description:
Following the reveal of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake earlier this year, Nintendo shared an extended look at the game during the company's latest Direct. Naturally, players have been sharing their opinions on social media, and certain aspects of the game's art style has been divisive among the fan base. However, there have been some very positive reactions as well.

The new looks for young Link and some of the other character inspired a round of memes and jokes.
title: The Internet Reacts To Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s Changes

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 looks to be a faithful remake in a lot of ways, with some light modernization touches here and there. The story as we've seen it also looks very faithful, from the Great Deku Tree to the fearsome appearance of Ganondorf. But among the quick flashes of story sequences one character in particular caught my eye, and it made me wonder if this remake will be more overt with one of the series' most famous twists.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time spoilers follow.

Ocarina of Time has a significant time jump, from child Link to adult Link, which earned this version of Link the nickname The Hero of Time. The child Link last saw Princess Zelda being spirited away from the castle by her bodyguard, Impa, during an apparent power grab by the evil Ganondorf. When Link takes the Master Sword and awakens as an adult, the castle i
title: Is The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Even Bothering With Its Big Twist?

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
There's no denying that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake looks weird. Whether you think it skews too far into the direction of realism or you're bawling your eyes out over how good Hyrule looks all these decades later, it's strange to see such a distinct and recognizable game look like this. And I'm hoping that it's received well, because I would love to see the same treatment applied to Ocarina of Time's incredibly strange and dark sequel, The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, if only too see just how messed up that moon is going to look.

It's possible you've never played Majora's Mask but will immediately recognize one of its primary antagonists: a menacing and ever-present moon that is slowly hurtling towards Clock Town over the span of three days. As time progresses, its creepy grin edges closer and closer to the ground, a constant reminder of the impending doom that only you can stop. It's a striking desi
title: We Need To See How Messed Up Majora’s Mask’s Moon Will Be In Ocarina of Time’s New Art Style

author: S.E. Doster
description:
The final season of Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 arrives on September 17, and Activision has revealed a Doom crossover event and shop bundle. Players can earn free rewards themed around the franchise, and there are also several paid cosmetics as well. All of these new Call of Duty Doom skins are highlighted below.

Starting on September 24, Call of Duty Season 6 will introduce a limited-time Doom event. This gives players the opportu
title: Check Out Call Of Duty’s Doom Skins In Black Ops 7 And Warzone

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits. Not every game publisher is on board with it, it seems, as Xbox users are reporting that four of the biggest companies aren't "participating" at all.

So far, it looks like games from Sega, Square Enix, Ubisoft, and Bandai Namco are largely incompatible with the disc-to-digital service. As verified by Kotaku, popping in a disc for a game from one of those publishers could result in a "not participating in digital licensing" message
title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Has A Big Problem: Several Major Publishers Aren’t Participating

author: Jean-Luc Seipke
description:
If you ask any retro nerd enthusiast like me what's the best way to experience classic gaming consoles, they're always going to start yapping at you about CRTs. And for good reason: CRTs offer zero input latency, variable refresh rate, and the best picture quality for viewing classic games. Many games designed their art around the visual intricacies of these old tube TVs to create transparent effects or blend colors to create detail not present when viewed as sharp pixels.

But CRTs in 2026 come with a lot of problems. They are hard to find and can
title: This Fake CRT TV Is A Brilliant Idea That Fails In The Most Essential Way

author: Alan Wen
description:
Nintendo's Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct has given us the first gameplay deep dive, showing how the 1998 N64 classic has been updated for Nintendo Switch 2, from a new detailed art style to new control additions like a jump button and motion-control aiming. However, from this first look, it also looks like the game will be sticking closely, if not identically, to the original game's layout.

The environments shown in the starting Kokiri Forest area are a lot more detailed, and you can now see them from a new perspective thanks to a free rotating camera. However, you can also see that the minimap the bottom-right of the screen shows the layout of the area is almost identical to the original game.

Glimpses of the first dungeon, Inside The Great Deku Tree, also have
title: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Map And Level Design Looks Quite Similar To The Original So Far

author: Jade King
description:
Grand Theft Auto has always had a complicated relationship with women. For decades, it’s been known as the series where you can visit a strip club, hire a sex worker, and swiftly beat her to death in the nearest alley. Violence against women in virtual settings praised for their unflinching realism is frequently turned into a punchline players are expected to chuckle at again and again and again. With the series achieving mainstream global stardom at a time when the medium was still predominantly an archaic boy’s club, it’s no surprise it has stuck around. 

But with the arrival of player character Lucia Caminos in the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 later this year, Rockstar has an opportunity to completely redefine the franchise’s problematic dynamic with women and potentially introduce one of the strongest female protagonists this medium has
title: After Decades Of Making Us Play As Men, GTA 6’s Lucia Has A Lot To Prove

author: Jason Fanelli
description:
Magic: The Gathering's final in-universe expansion of the year, Reality Fracture, is a consequential one for the lore of MTG. The current story arc, in which longtime hero Jace Beleren has become the overarching villain, reaches its conclusion here, and with Jace playing such a pivotal role in the story, it makes sense that he also plays a major part in the cards.

In fact, Jace is the focus of a new mechanic debuting in Reality Fracture, one that lead designer Mark Rosewater has been hyping up since MagicCon Atlanta in September 2025. That mechanic, as announced today during the Reality Fracture reveal stream, is the Jace Token, a new type of token that focuses on Planeswalker abilities. Here's how the token works.
title: Here’s How Jace Tokens Work In Magic: The Gathering’s Reality Fracture Expansion

author: S.E. Doster
description:
The final season of Black Ops 7 arrives next week, and the big update includes Call of Duty's annual The Haunting event. Spooky season starts early for Call of Duty in Season 6, with Black Ops and Warzone getting Halloween-themed operators, and there's even a limited-time Doom crossover event.

Call of Duty Season 6 start times

Seaso
title: CoD: Black Ops 7 And Warzone Season 6 Release Date And Details, Including Doom Crossover

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Retailer GameStop has released its latest earnings report, and it was a record-breaker for the company. The Texas-based retailer's biggest number for its fiscal Q2 quarter that ended August 1 was $160.2 million. That's how much GameStop made in operating income for the period, and it was the highest Q2 operating income level since the company went public in 2002.

Net income was up, too, reaching $298.7 million, compared to $168.6 million last year.

GameStop benefitted from continued growth in its biggest sales category--collectibles--which saw net sales jump a whopping 57% year-over-year to $356.3 mill
title: GameStop Sets A New Financial Record, And It’s No Thanks To Games

author: Cameron Koch
description:
BlizzCon 2026 begins September 12, and while there is big news every time developer Blizzard decides to host its fan convention, after a two-year hiatus, this year's show in particular seems poised to be a major occasion for fans of Blizzard franchises like Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch.

Blizzard president Johanna Faries hasn't been shy about hyping up this year's show in interviews, calling 2026 Blizzard's "biggest year yet." She said its various development teams are "cooking on big swings" across its key franchises and that this year's BlizzCon will reflect the studio's goal of being the "best gaming and entertainment company in the world." BlizzCon's announcements will deliver the "heart and soul" of what fans want out of a BlizzCon, she said, while still "bringing
title: What To Expect From BlizzCon 2026: StarCraft’s Return, A Whole Lot Of Warcraft

author: Erick Tay
description: Check out 9 minutes of gameplay featuring different weapons in Gundam Rogue Orbit from the Assault Sword to the Wipe Sword. Enjoy the action against smaller foes and mini bosses in missions.
title: 9 Minutes of Gundam Rogue Orbit Gameplay (Assault Sword, Sword Lance, Wipe Sword)

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda Direct was chock full of new details on the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, which composed the bulk of the presentation. That included a couple of new Amiibo figurines to collect, with some, uh, questionable in-game rewards.

The Amiibo themselves are figurines of young Link and young Zelda, and they are appropriately very cute. Link gazes up at Navi perched on his hand, while Zelda sits with her Ocarina. There's a lovely degree of detail. They'll be available in 2027, well after the remake actually hits Switch 2 this November.

Scanning them in-game, though, grants you the dubious reward of masks modeled after their original, more polygonal-forward N64 models. And friends, those faces on young Link's new body is a harrowing sight.
title: These Horrifying Ocarina Of Time In-Game Masks Are Your Prize For Buying New Zelda Amiibos

author: Jason Fanelli
description: Today, Nintendo aired The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. We learned the Ocarina of Time remake is launching November 5. We heard about a new orchestra concert touring the world in 2027. We finally got to see the title of the upcoming full-length movie: The Legend Of Zelda (no, really, that's it). Then, Eiji Aonuma walked us through a 15-minute gameplay demo of the upcoming Ocarina of Time Remake, and while the game's new look and gameplay are already being
title: Stop The Presses, Link Can Jump In Ocarina Of Time Remake

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
If you were hoping to see older Zelda games ported to or remastered for the Switch at the recent Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, you were likely disappointed, as Nintendo instead dedicated almost the entire show to its upcoming Ocarina of Time remake.

Out of all the Legend of Zelda remasters that have come to Switch consoles over the years, there's still a sizable Wind Waker HD-shaped hole in that collection. The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD released on the Wii U in 2013, with a number of upgrades compared to the original 2003 GameCube version.

While the original version of Wind Waker was added to the
title: The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Missed A Giant Wind Waker-Sized Opportunity

author: Alan Wen
description:
The remake for Zelda: Ocarina of Time isn't just a modern visual upgrade of the classic N64 game; it also makes use of a modern hardware feature, one that is built-in with the Switch 2 console.

As shown during The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct's first gameplay deep dive, you will be able to play Link's iconic ocarina not just with button inputs but also with your own voice humming the melodies of songs like "Zelda's Lullaby".

While the Switch 2's built-in mic was originally designed for GameChat, the system's integrated voice
title: The Ocarina Of Time Remake Has The Coolest Use Of The Switch 2’s Built-In Mic

author: Jessica Cogswell
description: The Legend of Zelda's 40th Anniversary Direct brought with it many exciting announcements, including a title reveal for the upcoming film and a release date for The Ocarina of Time remake. But while both of these were fairly predictable announcements, no one could have prepared me for what director Eiji Aonuma oh-so-casually slipped in directly proceeding his demonstration of the game: The Ocarina of Time's remake will featur
title: The Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Adding Something We Never Saw Coming: Voice Acting

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
After months of rumors, Nintendo finally revealed that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was real back in June. While that reveal was purely cinematic, today's Nintendo Direct for The Legend of Zelda showed off gameplay for the remake and offered a closer look at its updated art direction.

The Switch 2 exclusive stays true to the 1998 original's aesthetics, while showcasing a huge upgrade visually. Link's hat and tunic, for example, showcase detailed threading and embroidering, along with berries on his cap. The lighting system looks fantastic, too, as sunlight pokes through the forest as Link heads to the Great Deku Tree.
title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Looks Fantastic In First Gameplay Look

author: Chris Compendio
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 looks like a very faithful remake of the Nintendo 64 classic, but as seen in the Zelda 40th anniversary Direct, this updated version of the game takes at least one element from the modern open-world Zelda games.

When demonstrating the returning Fairy Slingshot item, Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma showed off the weapon-switching and aiming mechanics, which look nearly identical to the same systems in Breath of the Wild.

Players can quickly swap their weapons in a horizontal menu similar to the
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Borrows At Least One Mechanic From Breath Of The Wild

author: S.E. Doster
description:
The v1.0.4 update has arrived to Palworld, and the patch notes from Pocketpair reveal the addition of two new sub-missions, a much-needed search feature, and improvements to the game's fishing mechanic. 

Palworld's v1.0.4 adds two sub-missions for a continuation of the game's narrative. Players can access "Beyond Dimensions" by interacting with an NPC at Fisherman's Point in Mount Obsidian, and "From the Far Side of the Moon" is gained after clearing the previous mission.

The patch notes contain several new adjustments and bug fixes, but one of the most notable is the new search feature for the game's Palpedia. Palworld's list of Pals has continue
title: Palworld Update Adds New Missions And A Much-Needed Feature

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda Direct today spent the vast majority of its time showing off the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake, with loads of new details and an extended look at its revised art style. One change is likely to have a big impact on Ocarina fans, and appropriately enough, it involves the passage of time.

While exploring Hyrule's castle town, series creator Eiji Aonuma pointed out that the sun was setting, which means that now time will continue to pass while you're in town. That's a marked change from the original Ocarina, when time would stand still in town. The drawbridge would be closed at night, preventing you from entering the town, so you've never really been able to explore it at night.
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Makes A Big Change To Time Passing

author: Tomas Franzese
description:
During The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, Nintendo confirmed that a worldwide 40th Anniversary Concert Tour will take place in 2027.

After an original opening arrangement kicked off the direct and the movie title was revealed, legendary Nintendo composer Koji Kondo showed up to announce The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Concert, which will tour across Japan, North America, Eu
title: The Legend Of Zelda Anniversary Concert Tour Coming In 2027

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
As part of the Zelda-themed Nintendo Direct today, Nintendo announced that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's new remake for Switch 2 will release on November 5. That's just before GTA 6 launches on November 19.

The Ocarina of Time remake will cost $70 for the physical edition and $60 for the digital version.

Nintendo also showed off the first gameplay of the remake, including the game's updated graphics, new features, and more. Nintendo said the game's visuals have been "completely overhauled down to the textures of each material."

What's more, Nintendo is promising "snappier and more sa
title: Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Release Date Is November 5, Just Before GTA 6

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
After teasing fans with a few images earlier this year, Nintendo finally gave a little more info about the Legend of Zelda live-action movie. Very little! We now have a final title, but Nintendo chose not to share any additional images or a trailer yet. The movie will release on April 30, 2027.

Series creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared briefly to share that the final title is simply The Legend of Zelda. He called attention to the lack of subtitle, and said that once you see the movie the simplicity of the title will make sense. The movie stars Bo Bragason (Zelda) and Benjamin Evan Ainsworth (Link).

"Once you've seen the film, you'll understand why there isn't a subtitle," Miyamoto said. "This is an original film based on the many sto
title: The Legend Of Zelda Movie, Based On The Legend Of Zelda, Is Called The  Legend Of Zelda

author: Miri Teixeira
description:
With Gundam Rogue Orbit, Bandai Namco has clearly decided colossal robot fighting suits need a glow-up for a new generation, while also trying very hard to appeal to long-time Gundam fans. For the most part, it works. That's perhaps due to not letting expectations stifle it: The story is new, the gameplay is fresh and dynamic, and even the suits are a little bit special. 

After my hands-on preview of Gundam Rogue Orbit at Gamescom, I spoke with Yuya Tomiyama and Serizawa Yoshiyuku, both producers on the new game, about where they drew the line between respecting old fans and fearlessly flying into a brand-new Gundam universe. What struck me the most was the emphasis the pair put on how difficult this had been. There were no quick decisions made in this regard, and seemingly no decisions made by people who didn't have a genuine love of Gundam and wanted to pay homage to life-long supporters.
title: Gundam Rogue Orbit Looks To Do Things “Anime Couldn’t Achieve”

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Electronic Arts utilizes generative AI systems in its suite of development tools, and now another example has come to light. John Buccigross, the ESPN personality who joined the in-game broadcast booth for NHL 27 this year, has revealed that EA Sports used generative AI to simulate his voice in some scenarios. The developers seemingly did not disclose this prior to launch.

He said on the Chirping Zebras podcast (via 23sabres) that the developers played some AI-produced lines back for him, and he said they were "pretty good."

However, he also recalled times when the AI tools didn't get things completely right, so a h
title: EA Used AI To Clone John Buccigross’ Voice In NHL 27

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
This year marks a major milestone for The Legend of Zelda IP, but one that has seemingly had very little fanfare from its parent company, Nintendo. That all changes today, as Nintendo is dedicating a whole Direct broadcast to its long-running tale of heroes in green, mythical items of power, and the titular princess Zelda. Nintendo has--as always--kept mostly quiet about what you can expect from today's look at The Legend of Zelda, but it did confirm that the show will run for around 30 minutes.

If we had to make a guess as to what you can expect to see today, we'd guess that new details on the remake of The Legend of Zelda:
title: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct: All The Biggest Announcements

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Director Zach Cregger is making one of 2026's most-anticipated video game movies in Resident Evil, but don't expect him to make another film based on a franchise again.

Speaking to Deadline, Cregger said, "I'm doing this [Resident Evil], and that's it for me. I'm not going to go tackle any other franchises."

Why? He said it's because he wants to "write whatever I want to write," as opposed to adhering to a specific franchise's
title: Resident Evil Director Says He Won’t Do A Franchise Movie Again

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The big September Nintendo Direct is right around the corner, and so far, the only thing that Nintendo has confirmed about it is that it'll run for 45 minutes. Beyond that, the company is keeping a tight lid on tomorrow's broadcast, where it's expected to make a few big reveals that could help soften the blow of a $50 increase to the Switch 2 console.

That hasn't stopped leakers from making some bold predictions, as one insider claims that we could finally see a new 3D Mario game revealed. Malo932--who correctly predicted the reveal of the recent Star Fox game and the remake of Ocarina of Time--also correctly revealed that two Nintendo D
title: Rumored 3D Mario Game Could Finally Be Revealed At Tomorrow’s Nintendo Direct

author: Callum Self
description:
After over a decade with no new entries, the Silent Hill franchise has been on a roll recently. Since 2024’s Silent Hill 2 remake brought the beloved, dread-inducing game back into the spotlight, the spin-off Silent Hill f took somewhat of a detour, taking the familiar atmosphere to 1960s Japan. Now, the upcoming Silent Hill Townfall is twisting the formula further, introducing a first-person perspective and taking us to a fictional town in Scotland. If you’re looking to be scared during the Halloween period, you can already score a discount on the latest entry before it’s even released.

The Silent Hill 2 remake and Silent Hill f prove that the series can still be popular, delivering some of the best horror games in recent years (so long as you forget Ascension and The Short Message exist). However, much like Resident Evil 7 brought back that series wit
title: Silent Hill Townfall Isn’t Even Out Yet, But You Can Already Pre-Order It For Less Before Halloween

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
A new Onimusha game hit PC and consoles last week, and so far, it looks like Capcom has yet another win on its hands. Onimusha: Way of the Sword sold 1 million copies on launch day--bringing lifetime sales for the franchise up to 10 million--which is pretty impressive for a series that has been dormant for the better part of 20 years. Commenting on the early sales milestone, Capcom said that it wants to repeat Onimusha's success with other games that haven't seen a new release in many years.

"In addition to regularly releasing major new titles each year, Capcom is focusing on reactivating IPs that haven't had a new title launch recently,"
title: Capcom Is Getting My Hopes Up For Devil May Cry 6 With Its Talk Of “Reactivating” Dormant Franchises
